content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body:
Hi,

Thank you for sending over the draft agreement. Before I sign, I'd like to propose two adjustments to specific clauses so the terms are more in line with the overall value of the work.

- The relevant clause sets an aggregate liability cap of fifteen million dollars for direct damages. Given that the total fees payable under the agreement come to roughly five million dollars, this cap is about three times the value of the work, which could leave me exposed to damages well beyond what the deal is worth. I would suggest the clause be revised to read: "THE LIABILITY OF A PARTY TO THE OTHER FOR DIRECT DAMAGES SHALL NOT EXCEED TWO TIMES THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAYABLE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT."

- The relevant clause carves out third-party claims for injury or damages to persons or tangible property directly caused by any product from the cap in this section, with no separate ceiling applied. In plain terms, a single property-damage suit by a third party could create unlimited exposure. I would suggest adding to the end of that carve-out: "WHICH SHALL BE SUBJECT TO AN AGGREGATE LIMIT EQUAL TO THE FIFTEEN MILLION DOLLAR CAP IN THIS SECTION."

Let me know if these work for you or if you'd like to talk through any of them further. I'm happy to jump on a call if that's easier.

Thanks,
